title: Risk and Response in Large Language Models: Evaluating Key Threat Categories

bias_targets.methodology: Clustering red-team dialogue transcripts into a 'Discrimination/Hateful' category using BERTopic, analyzing the preference model's average harmlessness scores, and evaluating LLM refusal/compliance rates using the Do-Not-Answer benchmark with and without jailbreak templates.

Identifying prompts related to racism and racial discrimination through topic modeling (e.g., BERTopic keyword extraction) to evaluate preference model harmlessness scores and LLM safety behavior as part of the broader Discrimination/Hateful risk category.

Extracting red-team transcripts targeting specific religious groups (such as Jewish and Muslim communities) via topic modeling to map them into the Discrimination risk category and measure how the reward model scores their harmfulness.

Using BERTopic clustering to identify red-team attacks involving homophobia and anti-LGBTQ sentiment, analyzing how these threats are scored by the preference model and handled by language model guardrails.
Clustering red-team prompts involving sexism and gender-based discrimination to assess reward model harmlessness evaluations and LLM response action categories.
Categorizing prompts containing fat-shaming and insults based on physical characteristics to evaluate preference model harmlessness scores and language model refusal rates.
